Name: fading_scaffold_light_deflection
Title: A Fading-Scaffold Learning Progression from Heuristic Acceleration to Geodesic Light Deflection via a Removable Effective Refractive Index
Experiment: We will conduct a multi-institution controlled study with 120 upper-division undergraduate physics majors who have completed multivariable calculus and special relativity but no general relativity. Participants will be randomly assigned after a stratified math pre-test to one of three conditions: (A) the original heuristic acceleration derivation only; (B) a traditional Schwarzschild-metric geodesic derivation; (C) the proposed three-stage fading-scaffold sequence with a temporary effective refractive index. Each condition will use three 90-minute active-learning studio sessions with matched worked examples and practice problems. Data collection includes: (1) a pre-test on mathematical prerequisites and Newtonian light-deflection reasoning; (2) an immediate post-test with quantitative problems (Sun deflection, deflection by a star with different mass/radius) and conceptual items (why the GR value is twice the Newtonian prediction); (3) a 6-week delayed retention test; (4) a transfer test with galaxy-cluster lensing and strong-field qualitative items. Metrics are normalized learning gain, Cohen's d effect sizes, a problem-solving rubric, a custom Gravitational Light Deflection Concept Inventory (GLDI) with reported reliability, and a 9-point cognitive load scale after each stage. Primary comparisons are C vs A (does the scaffold improve conceptual and transfer performance without sacrificing quantitative accuracy?) and C vs B (does the scaffold improve accessibility, self-efficacy, and retention compared with a formal geodesic-only route?). Planned ablations within C include: C-noBridge, which removes the effective refractive index stage; C-noFade, which presents all stages as full worked examples without progressive completion or removal of heuristic terms; and C-noSim, which removes the interactive visualization layer. Expected outcomes: C will show a significant advantage over A on conceptual transfer (d > 0.5) and over B on immediate quantitative accuracy and self-efficacy (d > 0.4); C-noBridge will show weaker conceptual linkage between scalar and metric reasoning; C-noFade will show lower delayed retention and transfer; C-noSim will show reduced engagement but not necessarily lower learning, isolating visual scaffolding as motivational rather than cognitive.
